DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

Say It to the Mirror

STS-MS7-L3-13001400-MSVPA-MMG-NAV-02 • MS Visual and Performing Arts: Music • Performance Decorum and Audience Etiquette
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Old American theaters like the Orpheum gave performers a mirror before they ever gave them a stage, because the mirror tells the truth about a bow, a collar, and a nervous face. Musicians in jazz halls, school gyms, and church basements all learned the same lesson: the room changes what counts as polite. A shout that lifts a crowd at an outdoor festival can stop a quiet concert cold.
If your band played the same set in a school gym instead of the Orpheum, which one of the three audience rules would you change, and why?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Nora doing?
Look at the picture. Explain what Nora is doing and why she uses the mirror, in two sentences. Use exact words.
2
What is Wyatt holding?
Look at the picture. Explain what Wyatt holds and why he holds it now, in two sentences. Name it exactly.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Explain what the teacher is doing and why, in two sentences. Name the tool exactly.
4
What kind of place is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Explain what kind of place this is and your evidence, in two sentences. Name exact clues.
5
Tell me about this wall.
Look at the picture. Explain what the wall shows and its purpose, in two sentences. Use the exact printed words.
6
Tell me about what June is wearing.
Look at the picture. Explain what June wears and why it suits the concert, in two sentences. Use exact words.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
